glossary: pan de masa madre → sourdough bread
pan de espelta y nueces → spelt and walnut bread (nueces = walnuts)
pan de centeno → rye bread
(pan) semillas → seeded (bread)
tostada integral → wholemeal toast (British 'wholemeal', not 'whole wheat')
1/2 tostada / media → half toast; entera → whole
tomate (breakfast topping) → tomato; kept plain, not glossed as 'grated tomato with olive oil', because the source names only tomato and the rules forbid adding ingredients
tomate o mermelada y mantequilla → 'tomato, or jam and butter' (comma added so it can't be read as tomato-or-jam, plus butter)
paleta ibérica → Iberian cured shoulder (not ham leg); paleta (bocadillo, no 'ibérica') → cured shoulder (paleta)
vaso de fruta → fruit pot (avoided 'fruit cup', which in British English can mean a Pimm's-style drink); vaso (variant) → pot
licuado → juice blend (fresh juice from a juicer, as opposed to zumo = squeezed juice); used consistently in breakfast, set menus and the juice section
Combo (breakfast variant) → Combo (kept as is)
Merienda → kept in Spanish, glossed as the Spanish afternoon snack
Cacaolat → kept as brand name, glossed 'chocolate milk'
bizcochitos mini → mini sponge cakes
Menús de mediodía → Set lunch menus; Menú Básico / Completo → Basic / Full Set Menu; variant Menú → Set menu
Suplemento → Supplement (normal on British set menus)
tosta → open toast (section title, set-menu copy); item names shortened to 'Salmon/Avocado/Hummus toast'
pollo braseado → grilled chicken ('braseado' means cooked over embers; the British 'braised' is a false friend)
canónigos → lamb's lettuce
lechuga romana → romaine lettuce (also called cos in the UK)
lechugas variadas → mixed lettuce; mezcla de lechugas y brotes → mixed lettuce and shoots
mézclum → mixed leaves
picatostes → croutons
crujiente de yuca → crispy cassava
ventresca de atún → tuna belly (ventresca); salad and sandwich names kept as 'Ventresca' because that is the house name
maíz dulce → sweetcorn
cebolla morada → red onion; cebolla tierna → spring onion
pepinillos en vinagre → pickled gherkins
tomate seco → sun-dried tomato
rúcula → rocket
salsa especial «ranchera» → special 'ranch' dressing (British single quotes)
salsa César → Caesar dressing; salsa pesto → pesto
mix de frutos secos → mixed nuts (listed separately from walnuts, as in the source)
queso de cabra → goat's cheese
Bahía / Ambra (salad names) → kept as proper names
Ensalada Quinoa description 'Quinoa, hummus … y sésamo' → ellipsis kept because the source list is partly illegible
ensaladas note says 'six salads' although eight are listed: translated as written, not corrected
rosquilletas → kept, glossed 'Valencian breadsticks'
pimentón dulce → sweet paprika; garbanzos → chickpeas
pan de molde → sliced bread; pan de molde de tritordeum → tritordeum sliced bread (tritordeum is a wheat-barley hybrid grain; not glossed in the copy)
jamón York → cooked ham; jamón (focaccia, pizza, croissant, napolitana) → ham (source doesn't say cured or cooked)
a la plancha → griddled ('Griddled ham and cheese sandwich' rather than 'toastie', which implies a sandwich press)
bocadillo → kept in Spanish, glossed 'Spanish baguette sandwich'
atún y aceite → tuna and oil (source does not specify olive oil)
tiques → till receipts / receipts
Bollería del obrador → Pastries from our bakery (obrador = the café's own bakery)
vitrina → display counter / counter; vitrina refrigerada → chilled display case
Unidad → Each; Ración → Portion; Porción → Slice; Tableta → Bar; Taza → Cup; Vaso (coffee) → Glass; Botella → Bottle
Ensaimada → kept, glossed 'Mallorcan spiral pastry dusted with icing sugar'; Ensaimada Plus → kept, and 'Plus' is not explained because the source doesn't say what it means
Panquemao → kept, glossed as Valencian brioche-like sweet bread with a sugar-crusted top
caracola de chocolate → chocolate swirl
palmera de chocolate → chocolate palmier
Panut (dónut de la casa) → Panut (house doughnut); variants Blanco / Colores → White / Coloured
empanadillas → kept, glossed 'baked turnovers'; Pisto → kept, glossed 'Spanish-style ratatouille'
Peperoni → Pepperoni (English spelling); Verduras → Vegetable
napolitana → kept, glossed as a flat rectangular pastry made with croissant dough
San Marcos → kept, glossed as sponge cake with whipped cream and chocolate truffle, topped with caramelised egg yolk
coca de calabaza → kept, glossed 'Valencian pumpkin sponge cake'
Turrones → Turrón (singular Spanish form in the English name), glossed as Spanish nougat
P / G (juice sizes) → Small / Large; the note keeps P (pequeño) / G (grande) to explain the board
Licuado digestivo → Digestive juice blend (literal; context stops it being read as the biscuit)
Todos a (smoothie price label) → All at
café solo → Espresso
cortado → kept, glossed 'espresso with a dash of milk'
café con leche → kept, glossed 'espresso with hot milk'; Normal / Grande → Regular / Large
café bombón → kept, glossed 'espresso with sweetened condensed milk'
ColaCao → kept as brand name, glossed 'Spanish cocoa drink'
infusiones → herbal teas; té moruno → Moroccan tea; poleo → pennyroyal; poleo menta → pennyroyal mint; manzanilla → camomile (British spelling)
bebida de avena → oat milk (normal British café wording); corto → short; leche muy caliente → extra-hot milk; Sin cargo → No charge
IVA incluido → including VAT
refresco → soft drink; Agua (botella) → Bottled water
Prices in running text use English format: 0,20 € → €0.20, 5,xx € → €5.xx
